Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a left wrist injury, subsequently diagnosed as a
distal radius fracture. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported focre of the impact and the pattern of
the fracture. Over seven visits, care followed a typical course, beginning with immobiilzation and progressing to
supervised range-of-motion exercises as healing advanced. Visit frequency decreased steadily as symptoms
improved and the patient returned to daily activities. Examination findings included localized tenderness and reduced
grip strength that support the diagnosis, while neurovascular testing and sensation remained within normal limits.
Review of the available history found no prior injury to the left wrist or forearm. Billing records reflect single charges
for each service rendered, with no duplicate entries. Prognosis for full functional recovery is good, with follow-up
recommended if residual stiffness persists.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
